scope: Chat nickname entry, local composer behavior, preserving reading position, and an explicit return-to-latest control. No protected player, media values, backend, or actual app files were changed.

researchStatus.soopDedicatedHelpArticle: No indexed nickname/chat article was found from targeted help.sooplive.co.kr and help.sooplive.com searches. Official public player HTML was used as the SOOP evidence instead of claiming a help article had been read.

sources.title: 치지직 활동 닉네임 안내
sources.access: Web search followed by direct page open/find
facts: CHZZK activity names are managed through the Naver Game profile.
The guide describes name duplication rules and a 30-day change interval after the first immediate change.
sources.applied: Use a clearly named nickname-change entry and a distinct input/validation/save/cancel flow.
sources.notApplied: FRAME does not claim CHZZK account integration, nickname availability checks, or a 30-day change restriction.

sources.title: 라이브 채팅 이용 안내
sources.access: Web search followed by direct page open
facts: The guide separates participation/login requirements from viewing the chat.
Chat collapse, chat modes and chat rules are separate controls with different user/manager purposes.
sources.applied: Retain the prototype's existing login participation UI and chat-collapse flow. Improve only the local participant name and composer/read-position controls.
sources.notApplied: No moderator permissions, chat restrictions, login guarantees, rule agreement policy or cooldown policy were added.

sources.title: SOOP official public player
sources.access: Direct web page open after official-domain search. The retrieved response was in English; Korean menu strings also appeared in search-indexed official player responses.
facts: The public player response includes personal chat settings and a Change Nickname entry.
The response includes a separate Scroll down in chat button.
The name-change template has an input and separate cancel/change actions.
sources.applied: Provide an explicit name-change action and an explicit latest-message return control while preserving the existing chat layout.
notVerified: No logged-in SOOP nickname change was submitted.
The exact live behavior while scrolling away from the bottom was not interactively observed.
A public HTML template does not establish which controls are enabled for a specific account or broadcast.

sources.title: SOOP official public player, Korean indexed response
sources.access: Web search and direct open of an offline official player page
facts: The official player text separates personal settings, nickname change, chat display settings and the composer.
sources.notVerified: The offline template was not treated as a live authenticated UI test or as evidence of server behavior.

existingImplementationObservedInSource.finding: F.chat renders the name-change entry twice and maps every session message to the current F.nickname whenever the view is rebuilt.
The old chat submit handler appends a local string message and always sets scrollTop to scrollHeight, even when the user was reading earlier messages.
Logged-out participation is already replaced with a login entry; this behavior is retained.
Existing nickname validation and modal navigation are local prototype behavior, separate from actual account/session APIs.

designDecisionsAndAssumptions.decision: The visible action combines the current local nickname with a concise 변경 action, and the modal is called 채팅 닉네임 변경.
designDecisionsAndAssumptions.reason: This makes the action explicit without claiming that the account profile nickname is being edited.

designDecisionsAndAssumptions.decision: Keep 1–20-character validation and show no nickname-availability or change-cooldown claim.
designDecisionsAndAssumptions.reason: The existing prototype can validate local input but has no authoritative account/name registry.

designDecisionsAndAssumptions.decision: When more than 24px above the chat bottom, keep the reading position and display 최신 메시지로. Follow new appended messages only while already following the bottom.
designDecisionsAndAssumptions.reason: This preserves the user's reading intent. The SOOP source establishes a return-to-bottom control, while the exact follow/threshold implementation is a FRAME design choice.

designDecisionsAndAssumptions.decision: Snapshot the display name at actual local submission; changing the local chat name affects later submissions and does not rewrite prior authors.
designDecisionsAndAssumptions.reason: A visual change must not make earlier messages appear to have a different author. This is display metadata, not an authenticated identity guarantee.

implementation.loadOrder: After foundation and before the root reference/detail wrapper; before design-events.js is suitable.

stateFields.rooms: Map of per-view/channel scroll state {top, follow, lastHeight}
stateFields.authors: Display-name snapshots aligned with the existing local session message array
stateFields.name: Local modal draft, inline error, editing flag and first-open selection flag
stateFields.channels: Map of local per-broadcast message arrays and original author names; channel 0 is shared by its sender and viewer views
stateFields.activeChannel: Local broadcast currently bound to F.sessionMessages

preserved: Existing chat fixtures, chat-collapse controls and participant login UI
Enter to send, Shift+Enter for a line break, and IME composition protection
Existing 1,000-character input limit without adding a visible fixed counter
All player, quality, source video, media settings, backend and actual application files
changed: One clear current-name/change entry instead of a duplicate bare pencil action
A draft-based nickname modal with unchanged-value disabling, validation, cancel and explicit change submission
Input autosizing without a resize handle; disabled empty send action and inline over-limit feedback only when necessary
Per-view scroll restoration on re-render, contained chat scrolling and return-to-latest control
Mutation observation of real appended chat-line elements; no fabricated incoming message or participant-count events
Stable nickname-trigger ID restores focus after a successful rename
Chat-log keyboard focus prevents Space/k/m/t/f from activating player shortcuts
Local messages and author snapshots are isolated per broadcast; sender/viewer of channel 0 share the same local history

validation.browserQA: Integrated root browser checks completed; see browser-summary.json. Physical devices and real network delivery remain untested.
scenarios: Open the current-nickname 변경 action, submit an empty value, correct the error, cancel and verify the committed name is unchanged.
Submit a local message, change the name, submit another message, re-render and verify both original author names remain.
Submit enough real local test messages to create overflow; scroll upward, send/append another real message and verify the reading position remains stable.
Use 최신 메시지로, verify the bottom is reached and the control disappears.
Toggle a surrounding view or open/close a modal while reading old chat and verify the scroll position is restored.
Verify empty send disabling, Shift+Enter, IME Enter behavior, long-name truncation and mobile composer/button bounds.

remainingLimitations: Nickname state, message text, author snapshots and scroll positions exist only in the local prototype memory.
There is no server name-availability check, authenticated identity mapping, moderation policy or account-profile synchronization.
The local per-broadcast Map is not a server-backed chat store and does not survive a reload.
Real message delivery, acknowledgement, reconnection, deduplication and production incoming-event integration remain unimplemented.
No competitor account was logged into and no nickname/account setting was changed on CHZZK or SOOP.
